When I first started looking into getting new ultralight gear for my John Muir Trail/Whitney trip this summer, I wanted to get some quality gear, not just third-world made junk that would fall apart. I was bummed to see that there was seemingly not many choices for Made in the USA backpacking gear. Even REI didn’t have that much. But thanks to the internet I was able to find lots of newer companies making highly-rated gear for backpackers right here in the USA.

Backpack: ULA Catalyst (http://www.ula-equipment.com/))

Tent: Tarptent Double Rainbow (http://www.tarptent.com/))

Sleeping Pad: ThermaRest NeoAir Xlite (https://www.thermarest.com/))

Stove: MSR Windburner (http://windburnerstove.com/))

Bear Canister: Bear Vault BV500 (http://www.bearvault.com/))

Water Filter: Sawyer MiniFilter (https://sawyer.com/products/sawyer-mini-filter/))

Head lamp: Princeton Tec Remix (http://www.princetontec.com/))

GPS Rescue beacon: ResQlink ACR (www.acratex.com)

Hat: Henchel Hiking hat

Knife: Buck Spitfire

Trowel: Dutchware Deuce Scoop titanium (http://dutchwaregear.com))

Socks: Darn Tough Light Hikers (https://darntough.com/))

Stuff sacks: Z-packs (http://www.zpacks.com/))

The only major gear that I have that wasn’t made in America is my sleeping bag. I was able to get a REI bag basically for free from a co-worker. I’ll eventually get another bag, but this one will do fine for this trip.

Can't wait to get this stuff out on the trail.
